newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Banco de Boston shows no interest in Rio's Banerj.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Boston shows no interest in Rio's Banerj.

text.p: BankBoston's Brazil unit said it is not interested in Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj, despite changes in the bank's sales rules, a bank official said.

Banco de Boston, which had prequalified for the sale last year, but dropped out, continues to believe the purchase of Banerj would lead the bank to an excessive concentration "in a relatively small territory," said Augusto Nunes, Corporate Communications vice-president.
Banerj's branch network is concentrated in the southeastern state of Rio de Janeiro.
"If Banco de Boston buys Banerj, it would move its focus to a relatively small area," he said.
After failing twice in auctioning off its bank in 1996, Rio de Janeiro state now hopes to privatize Banerj on June 20 for a lower price of 300 million reais.

Banco de Boston was one of the seven financial institutions that had prequalified for Banerj's sale last year. But only two -- Bradesco and Banco Itau -- ended up signing up for the auction and were ready to bid.
According to the new rules, new investors can prequalify for the sale as of Wednesday, but already prequalified bidders do not have to prequalify again.
Nunes added that Sao Paulo state bank Banespa, which is now in federal hands and is expected to be privatized by November 1998, does not attract Banco de Boston either.

He said the bank eyes medium-sized banks. Banco de Boston has already prequalified for the sale of Minas Gerais state bank Credireal and aims to prequalify for the privatization of federal bank Meridional, he said.
